analysis.title: Cloud Solutions Architect
analysis.fit_rationale: The candidate has strong infrastructure, capacity planning, performance engineering, and Python automation experience, with some AWS project exposure and practical AI skills. However, the role demands deep cloud-native architecture expertise, formal architecture artifacts, stakeholder management, and 13+ years of experience, which the candidate's profile only partially covers. The candidate's cloud experience is project-based (AWS lakehouse) and foundational (Azure), not professional production architecture. The candidate's current role is capacity/performance specialist, not architect. The score reflects a moderate fit with clear gaps in formal architecture leadership and cloud-native design depth.
strengths: Expert-level Python, SQL, and ETL design from professional roles
Deep capacity planning and forecasting expertise (CITI, HorizonScale)
Performance engineering and APM experience (Dynatrace, CA APM)
Practical AI and automation skills (LLM agents, RAG, MCP)
Strong data engineering and pipeline monitoring background
gaps: No professional cloud architecture role or formal architecture artifacts
Cloud expertise is project-based (AWS) and foundational (Azure), not deep production architecture
Lacks cloud architecture certification (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
No experience with cloud migration, modernization, or platform consolidation programs
Limited stakeholder management and architecture review leadership evidence
No multi-cloud or hybrid cloud experience
tailoring_plan: 1. Rewrite resume summary to emphasize cloud architecture interest and relevant AWS project experience. 2. Add a 'Cloud Architecture Projects' section detailing the AWS lakehouse design, including S3, Glue, Athena, and Bedrock, and highlight architectural decisions (e.g., Parquet/Snappy optimization). 3. Emphasize any experience with containerization or serverless (if any) from projects or coursework; otherwise, consider upskilling. 4. Highlight Python automation and data pipeline skills as transferable to cloud architecture. 5. In the cover letter, address the gap in formal architecture roles
